blocks.title: Después de este pdf sabrás
bullets: reconocer los sustantivos contables e incontables
expresar cantidades con much, many, a lot of, a few, a little

blocks.text: Las palabras contables tienen plural: an apple, two apples. Las incontables no: water, money, information. No llevan a ni an, ni -s, y el verbo va en singular.

blocks.title: Incontables en inglés, contables en español
Un consejo = a piece of advice
blocks.text: Para una unidad de algo incontable se dice a piece of: a piece of advice (un consejo), a piece of furniture (un mueble), a piece of news (una noticia). Y además: Your hair is long (tienes el pelo largo); The news is good (las noticias son buenas); I need some information, nunca informations.

head: Uso
Ejemplo
rows: There is some milk. I've got some friends here.
Would you like some tea? Can I have some water?
There isn't any milk. I haven't got any money.
Are there any shops near here?
There's no milk. = There isn't any milk.

blocks.title: something, anything, nothing
blocks.text: La misma regla vale para something / anything / nothing, somebody / anybody / nobody y somewhere / anywhere / nowhere: I didn't see anything. Is anybody there? There's nobody here. Ojo: el inglés no tiene doble negación: No vi nada = I didn't see anything o I saw nothing, nunca I didn't see nothing.

head: Contable
Incontable
Ejemplo
rows: How many people? Not much time.
a lot of friends, a lot of money
a few days, a little sugar
How many eggs? How much milk?

blocks.title: How much is it? — ¿Cuánto cuesta?
blocks.text: Con los precios se usa siempre How much, aunque cuentes euros: How much is it? How much does it cost?

head: Ejemplo
Español
rows: There's too much sugar. There are too many cars.
Tiene demasiado azúcar. Hay demasiados coches.

blocks.title: too es demasiado, no muy; enough va detrás del adjetivo
blocks.text: too significa demasiado, con un sentido negativo: It's too hot = hace demasiado calor (es un problema). Para muy se dice very: It's very nice, nunca It's too nice. Y enough va detrás de un adjetivo (big enough = lo bastante grande), pero delante de un sustantivo (enough money = dinero suficiente).

rows: Can you give me an advice?
Can you give me some advice?
I have a lot of friends.
En una frase afirmativa: a lot of.

blocks.text: Completa con la palabra correcta. Las respuestas están en la última página.

items.full: How much sugar do you want?
How many brothers have you got?

items.q: Can I have ______ milk in my tea?
items.full: Can I have a little milk in my tea?

items.q: This bag is ______ heavy. I can't carry it.
items.full: This bag is too heavy. I can't carry it.
He isn't old enough to drive.

items.q: She gave me a good piece of ______.
items.full: She gave me a good piece of advice.
Is there anything in the fridge?
The news is very good today.

items.q: There were ______ many people at the party.
items.full: There were too many people at the party.

items.a: Can you give me some advice?
